newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds little changed, Flagstar pops.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds little changed, Flagstar pops.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds endured another dull session on Tuesday as interest rate uncertainties sidelined investors, and prices ended little changed, dealers said.

High-yielding activity, meanwhile, was dominated by a 10-point boost ot senior subordinated debt of Flagstar Cos Inc following an announcement of a restructuring agreement that would convert that debt to a 95.5-percent equity stake.
The rest of the high-yield market failed to shake a softer tone seen since last week and prices were mostly flat to marginally weaker, dealers said.
Telecommunication sector debt, which has taken the brunt of selling over the past week, was mixed on the day. Traders said some of the hardest hit bonds have stemmed their slide.

Adelphia Communications Corp's $350 million 9-7/8 percent 10-year debt was steady on Tuesday at 92, but remained well below its late February issue price of 99.217, a trader said. The Adelphia debt fell about one point on Monday.

Nextel Communications Inc, which reported a fourth quarter loss last week, weakened. Nextel zeros due 2004 extended their slide and fell 1/2 to 3/4 point on Tuesday to 69-1/2 bid, 70 offer, after a 3/4 point drop on Monday.
"People are beginning to lighten up," one trader said. "On top of that (buy-siders) are being more selective, they're not spending cash as freely as they used to."

Even with the weakness elsewhere, traders called Flagstar's senior subordinated debt most active on Tuesday and the 11-3/8s due 2003 rose to 45 in a short-covering rally. The senior notes, which would receive a lower coupon and extended maturity in the restructuring, rose 1/2 point to 98-1/2.
In new issuance, heavy machinery wheel and tire maker Titan Wheel International Inc headed an expected $1.5 to $2.0 billion week subordinated notes.
The B1/BB-minus rated notes weres priced as 8-3/4s to yield 8.825 percent or 210 basis points over the curve. The deal was quoted at issue bid of 99-1/2 near the close.
Merrill Lynch & Co Inc was lead manager on the deal.

Elsewhere, Yankee issuer petroleum exploration and production concern Gulf Canada Resources Ltd issued $225 million 8-1/4 percent 20-year senior notes to yield 8.265 percent or 125 basis points over the curve.
The Ba1/BB-plus rated issue was managed by a Goldman, Sachs & Co syndicate.

High-grade issuance was led by $360 million 7-1/2 percent 10-year senior unsecured notes to yield 7.597 percent or 88 basis points over the Treasury curve. The Baa3/BBB-minus rated issue, priced via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, was increased in size by $60 million, the dealer said.
Secondary activity remained transfixed with next week's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting and upcoming inflation data, traders there said. Spreads were considered flat on the day.
"The market really didn't do anything significant today because people want to see what the (Consumer Price Index) is going to bring (Wednesday), a retail industrials trader said.

A narrowly traded U.S. Treasury market, which briefly traded off following a strong housing starts report, dictated the somnambulant tone in corporates, traders said. The 30-year bond closed down 2/32 at 95-25/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
